sources.note: Lexicon sourced solely from Conrad & Dye (1975); no stress marking, no prosody.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Amto language' and 'Amto-Musan languages' (raw wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Amto language' is a location stub (refs Ethnologue 25, UN village coordinates). The family page gives cognate tables from Foley 2018 and Conrad & Dye 1975 (via transnewguinea.org) and cites Usher's New Guinea World; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A40.1.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 Amto-Musan Family (pp. 19-20): speakers, villages, 29% cognates, sound correspondences (Amto u, o/a, k, p, n/r, h ~ Musan); no Amto phonology. The paper's only stress remark ('Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga', Figure C) is about the Arai/Left May family, not Amto. Amto otherwise appears only as a column in the comparative wordlists.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1975. Isolates: Sepik Region. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 879-886. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.15.1.2.4 AMTO (Ki), pp. 883-884: classification history only (Loving & Bass 1964 'Busa Phylum' rejected; 29% probable cognates with Musian per Conrad & Dye 1975; Bailey's wordlists); ends 'No data is available on typological features.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification (Pacific Linguistics B-25). Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/146478.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 209 AMTO (Ki): pop. 230; villages Amto, *Minor, *Wakumo; 'Wordlist N. J. Cavanagh (1961), SIL lists, wordlists by David Bailey (Green River), 1971'; bilingualism note. No phonology, nothing on stress. Entry 210 Musian: 'little other structural information is extractable from the data'.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Samaia River' and 'Amto' pages (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pages exist only as empty headings (raw export '====== Amto ======', 20 bytes); the Samaia River topic 'does not exist yet'. No data.
